newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian coffee prices inch up on NY hike.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian coffee prices inch up on NY hike.

text.p: Indonesian coffee prices inched up on Monday on the back of an increase in New York last Friday, with exporter-buying seen keeping values steady, traders said.
They said grade four Robusta was quoted at 2,700-2,800 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, up from 2,650-2,700 rupiah a week ago.
The traders said the export price fob Lampung was quoted at $1,230/tonne, up from last week's $1,200-$1,210.
"The gains in New York helped the market, but trading activity has mostly been scattered," one trader said. "I expect prices to remain stable through the week."
Coffee prices climbed to a fresh six-week high in New York on Friday as supply jitters pushed the benchmark December futures contract up 1.40 cents a lb to 116.30 cents.
London Robusta futures, however, ended mixed last Friday and traders there said values were mainly depressed by persistent Asian and African producer selling.

One local trader said there has been some steady buying by trading houses. "One trading house bought about 400 to 500 tonnes last week, while another has been buying 100 to 200 tonnes each day," one trader said.
He said some players who had sold forward were looking to cover their positions.
The trader said he expected New York prices to open steady later on Monday, but expected London Robusta values to ease.
"Vietnam is on the market, and this will likely keep London prices soft," he said. "There are also beans in the hands of Indonesian players, although the harvest is coming to a close."
